title: Create an event via left-click 'Create Event' on empty grid space
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit (event creation requires Edit; spec §14.1).
preconditions:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps:
1. Left-click an empty spot in a technician's cell on a working day (not on an existing block).
2. Choose 'Create Event' from the menu that opens.
3. Fill in a name (for example 'ZZAUTOTEST stand-up'), keep the date/times offered, and save.
expected:
1. A menu opens at the spot you clicked and contains 'Create Event'.
2. The event modal opens with the clicked cell's technician and date pre-set.
3. Saving creates an event block on that technician's day.
4. A toast with Undo appears.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8685 and the Schedule specification version 23 (§4.10, §7). Last checked against build v3.5-4873abe on 8/4/2026.

title: An event's hours count toward the capacity bar but raise no conflict
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars and Events are ON in View Options.
3. A technician has a shift and, on the same day/time, an event (create both, ZZAUTOTEST).
steps:
1. Note the day's capacity bar fill with only the shift present.
2. Add an all-day (or long) event on the same technician and day.
3. Look at the capacity bar again and check for any conflict on the block and in the toolbar conflict pill.
expected:
1. Adding the event DOES increase that day's capacity bar fill - the event's hours are counted alongside shift hours (a 2-hour meeting uses up 2 hours of the technician's available time).
2. The event does NOT create a double-booked or overlap conflict with the shift, and the toolbar conflict count does not increase because of it.
3. The two behave differently on purpose: an event uses up capacity, but it is never flagged as a conflict.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8685 and the Schedule specification version 23 (§4.10, §4.11, §4.12). Last checked against build v3.5-4873abe on 8/4/2026.

Verbatim: 'A) §4.12 PRD is explicit: "Event time is included in the utilization total alongside shifts, so meetings and training consume capacity." A 2-hour meeting consumes 2 hours of capacity. title: Before-hours and after-hours shifts are flagged against the tech's hours
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician has a known working day (for example 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM).

steps:
1. In day view, drag the shift so it starts BEFORE the technician's working-day start (for example 6:00 AM).

3. Now drag the shift's right edge so it extends PAST the working-day end (for example to 7:00 PM).

expected:
1. The shift is flagged as a before-hours conflict, with a reason sentence in the spirit of 'Starts before working hours', measured against that technician's own configured working-day START time (not a fixed hour).

3. Both the start and the end follow the hierarchy technician hours, then shop business hours, then the general default working day of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
4. Warning icon on the block in each case; the conflict appears in the toolbar dropdown.
